title: Hybrid routing long-span eviction casebook: Llama / Mistral / Qwen
body:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on casebook capturing experiment notes and reproducible traces for a recurring tail-latency/eviction pattern we observed when serving mixed-model MoE/FT (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) workloads with long-context sessions (>=32k tokens). Goal is to document observed behaviors, likely root causes, short-term mitigations we validated, and next engineering follow-ups.

Context / symptom summary (high level):
- Customer and internal synthetic workloads show p95/p99 latency spikes and sudden throughput collapse when long-context interactive sessions are mixed with short-turn requests on the same node pool.
- The spikes correlate with increased KV-cache evictions and large gating imbalance for MoE models. Effect appears stronger on 64k context windows and on models with sparse routing (32 experts).
- Affected models: Llama-2-70B (dense baseline for comparison), Mistral-7B (dense), Qwen-14B (sparse/MoE variant in these tests). We also ran a 2-expert hybrid expert model for verification.

How we reproduced (commands and quick repro):
- Reproducer harness is in gs://redwood-perf/runs/2025-01-11/hybrid-evict/. Key steps:
  1) Spawn a serving node with 4xA100 (80GB), server runtime branch: pr/1296 (includes extra eviction logging).
  2) Start 150 long-context sessions: prompt length 8k, append token stream to 64k using controlled generator (rate 50 t/s per session) while also sending short 16-token requests at 200 QPS.
  3) Measure per-request latency histograms, kernel stalls, NVLink bw, KV-cache eviction counters (runtime metrics: kv_evictions_total, kv_pin_count, gating_load_stddev).
- Reproducer cli: ./perf-harness --model qwen-14b-sparse --sessions 150 --long-window 65536 --short-qps 200 --duration 20m --collect-traces

Observed signals (empirical):
- p99 latency (qwen-sparse) increased from baseline ~290ms -> 1.2s during peaks. Llama and Mistral show smaller but notable p99 increases (Llama p99 220ms -> 480ms).
- kv_evictions_total spiked shortly before latency spikes. Evictions are primarily due to activation KV memory pressure rather than explicit explicit eviction policy triggers (i.e., memory usage climbed, runtime reclaimed KV pages).
- gating_load_stddev for Qwen-sparse increased by 3–5x (indicating heavy imbalance across experts).
- NVLink utilization concurrently spikes; DMA stalls on certain GPUs correlate with time windows when large expert fanouts occur.
- Historical server trace (trace id: run-2025-01-11-1542) shows long tail backpressure: stalled kernel queue times increase ~5x on GPUs hosting ‘hot’ experts.

Initial hypothesis (causal chain):
1) Long-context sessions keep large per-session KV caches pinned or frequently touched.
2) MoE routing produces episodic expert hotspots (skewed gating). When a hotspot aligns with many long-context sessions that reference the same token patterns, GPU local memory and NVLink DMA queues get saturated.
3) Saturation forces the runtime to evict KV pages (or shuffle pages across UVM/host), which produces I/O stalls and kernel page faults, adding 100s ms to p99.
4) Evictions also cause gating to re-balance poorly because some experts take longer to respond, which increases fanout and worsens imbalance — a positive feedback loop.

Key profiling artifacts (where to find them):
- Flame/trace: gs://redwood-perf/runs/2025-01-11/hybrid-evict/trace.json (big-steps: KV eviction events align with kernel queue backlog and NVLink transmit spikes).
- Per-GPU timeline: gs://redwood-perf/runs/2025-01-11/hybrid-evict/gpu-timelines/* (look for recurring DMA stall patterns).
- Kernel profiles (Nsight snapshots): linked in the run folder, see nsight-idx-09-11-2025.tar.gz.

Quantitative summary (selected numbers):
- Baseline steady-state (no long sessions): qwen-sparse p99 290ms, kv_evictions/hr ~ 2.
- With mixed long sessions: qwen-sparse p99 1.2s, kv_evictions/hr ~ 48 (mostly short-lived pages).
- Mitigation test (per-session KV pinning enabled): qwen-sparse p99 reduced to ~210ms but throughput fell by ~10% at burst load (due to higher reserved KV memory).
- Staggered prefetch (delaying prefetch by 20–50ms per session) reduced occurrence of simultaneous hot expert loads and cut p99 spikes by ~40%.

What we tried (quick experiments and outcomes):
- Per-session KV pinning: Pros — eliminates on-demand evictions for pinned sessions; Cons — raises steady memory footprint and reduces headroom for bursty traffic. Useful for customer-dedicated pools where capacity is overprovisioned.
- Soft routing cap: limit max fanout per request (drop lowest scoring experts beyond N). Reduced NVLink bursts and p99 by ~30% for Qwen sparse, but small accuracy loss on contrived prompts.
- Staggered prefetch: random jittering of prefetch windows across sessions; low implementation cost and consistent p99 reduction on mixed workloads.
- Local expert throttling: add per-GPU admission for expert calls; reduces hotspot saturation but increases request variance and sometimes increases P50.

Interpretation and recommended near-term mitigations (runtime):
- For hosted pools with heterogeneous session lengths, enable staggered prefetch by default and expose a per-pool toggle for "aggressive KV pinning" (enterprise/dedicated only).
- Add a short-term admission control that detects rising kv_evictions_total and engages a routing soft-cap (reduce max fanout from 32 -> 8) until memory stabilizes.
- Add NVLink / DMA stall metrics to auto-detect imminent hotspot events and correlate with gating skew. This will give early warning for rolling traffic to other nodes.

Longer-term engineering actions (design notes):
- Gating regularization: add a routing penalty for experts that are currently serving heavy backlog (cost-aware gating). That requires routing model changes and careful A/B.
- Work with compile/kernels team to reduce stall-sensitivity of expert dispatch (coalesce small expert kernels or use small-batch fused kernels when fanout is high).
- Per-session KV eviction profiler: runtime should track per-session eviction counts and surface sessions that cause churn. Use that in Console to suggest session pinning or session migration.
- Explore more fine-grained KV placement (partial pinning of recent KV slabs) instead of all-or-nothing pinning.

Open questions and notes: (for follow-up experiments)
- How much of this is model architecture vs input distribution? We saw strong signal from adversarial prompts that induce the same gating pattern across sessions; need to test with more realistic user prompts.
- Impact of quantization: we ran mixed-precision; quantized activations reduce memory but may increase time per kernel — tradeoff unclear.
- Node topology matters: we saw worse behavior when hot experts were collocated on GPUs sharing the same NVSwitch vs spread across PCIe domains. Need controlled topology sweep.

Next steps (actionable):
- (Week 1) Ship staggered prefetch and routing soft-cap to canary fleet; monitor kv_evictions_total and p99 for 2 weeks. (Owner: Liang)
- (Week 2) Implement NVLink/DMA stall alerts in the trace pipeline and add Console dashboard chart for kv_evictions_total / gating_skew. (Owner: Marisol)
- (Week 3) Prototype cost-aware gating in a feature branch and run offline evals on prompt corpus to estimate quality impact. (Owner: Samir)
- Document a recommended configuration for Dedicated customer pools that frequently run long-context sessions. (Owner: Ryan)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working-level doc; logs and full traces live in the linked run folder. If you want kernel-level slices, ping me (Samir) or Liang and I'll extract .nvpr files.
- If any SRE folks want to run topology sweeps, I can provide an orchestration script that pins experts to particular GPUs for more deterministic runs.

Appendix (quick pointers / reproducer flags):
- perf-harness flags used: --prefetch-delay-ms 0|20|50 --kv-pin={none,partial,full} --routing-cap={8,16,32} --topology-pin (affinity map file).
- Things to observe in traces: eviction_start timestamp, eviction_end, nvlink_dma_queue_depth, gating_scores_stddev, per-expert_inflight_count.

End of note.

(If you want a shorter summary for Slack / bug triage, I can extract a 6-line executive blurb.)
